parsed.explanation: The division's bathroom statute is the decisive traveller-facing exposure: it is enacted, reaches private businesses and hospitals, and carries up to a year in jail, while the pending suit is not a working remedy. National document rules add border refusal and possible lifetime fraud findings for sex-marker discrepancies, and immigration custody is documented as abusive; a visitor detained after a border or facility encounter faces birth-sex placement and severe harm. National hate-crime and employment protections and some court injunctions are real but do not reach the facility ban or border discretion. For a family with a trans minor, state disclosure duties and national care restrictions add forced outing and care-denial risk. The result is High Risk: above execution/routine-arrest anchors, but well below jurisdictions with functioning facility and border protections.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules require M/F birth sex on passports/visas; X markers are no longer issued; border cable permits refusal where documents or reasonable doubt on sex exist, and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility for suspected misrepresentation.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, and has limited waivers; passport policy is under legal challenge.
entry_documents.interaction: A foreign passport marker or appearance mismatch can trigger secondary inspection, refusal, or fraud referral; airline and border-officer discretion determines whether the visitor is stranded or admitted.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody documents forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men; national corrections policy mandates conversion-therapy-like treatment, hormone removal, and stops reporting trans prisoner numbers; a bathroom arrest analog was held in a men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; some executive orders are enjoined; a legal-aid FAQ exists, but no documented remedy changes custody practice.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border discrepancy can lead to detention and birth-sex custody; a local bathroom arrest can lead to jail and men's-ward placement; remedies are slow and not shown to alter conditions.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law criminalizes restroom or changing-room use not matching birth sex in government buildings and public-facing private businesses, including gas stations, restaurants, venues and hospitals; first offence up to one year. National facility bans cover many states/provinces.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No operative visitor-facing protection documented; suit filed 30 April 2026 and possible 16 June 2026 narrowing are unresolved; some other states/provinces have no ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The division's private-business reach is the harshest documented; a visitor using ordinary commercial or hospital facilities carries criminal exposure alongside national facility restrictions.

care_services.exposure: National orders restrict gender-affirming care for minors, describe it as mutilation, and propose insurance exclusions; division law requires schools, childcare and medical professionals to disclose a trans minor's status to parents within three days; hospital restrooms are covered by the criminal facility ban.
care_services.protection: Some national orders are enjoined; adult care is not shown banned; no documented visitor care denial in this division.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family seeking care or childcare for a trans minor risks forced parental disclosure and provider refusal; an adult visitor's care access is uncertain, and hospital restroom use is criminalized.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy lists 'radically pro-transgender' groups among priorities; justice-department reward guidance references 'radical gender ideology'; executive orders target teachers and schools; official rhetoric frames trans identity as ideology.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Guidance says counterterrorism will not target mere disagreement; courts have enjoined some orders; national hate-crime law exists.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile framing raises the risk that border, police or school officials treat visible trans status as a security or child-protection issue; local bathroom enforcement can invoke police.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division law requires schools, childcare and medical professionals to disclose a trans minor's status to parents within three days; national executive order directs prosecution of teachers using preferred names/pronouns; care bans exist in 27 states/provinces; the bathroom law applies to minors.
minors_guardians.protection: Some national orders are enjoined; state health-board rules retain parental, emancipation or court-order routes, but these are resident-facing and do not protect a visiting minor from disclosure.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans minor travelling with guardians can be outed to parents by a clinic, childcare or school; an unsupportive guardian creates captivity or abuse risk, while provider liability can deny care.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific trans violence rate above the general homicide rate is documented; national hate-crime law covers gender identity, but only 23 states/provinces have bias statutes; police enforcement of a bathroom law produced handcuffing and arrest in an analogous state.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute; 22 states/provinces plus the capital district outlaw gender-identity discrimination; civil-rights litigation exists.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Where local bias statutes are absent, harassment or refusal may be under-remedied; police called to enforce the bathroom law can become the outing, arrest or violence vector.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: The bathroom-law suit is unresolved; a possible 16 June 2026 narrowing is unconfirmed; the passport/fraud policy is challenged but operative; custody-abuse oversight is not shown to remedy the practice.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-rights suit filed; some executive orders enjoined; legal-aid FAQ; national hate-crime and employment protections; existing X passports remain valid.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Court remedies are prospective and slow; they do not block a present facility arrest, border fraud discretion, or abusive custody, so the traveller faces the operative rules now.

anchor_checks.comparison: Varnalia's decency statute, routine arrests for presentation, months of pretrial beatings, compelled confessions and capital exposure are materially worse. Here the criminal statute is facility-specific, no execution or routine presentation arrests are documented, and courts have blocked some national orders. This dossier sits above 0.15-A.

Ostravia's birth-sex prison housing, cross-dressing ban in administrative buildings, frequent assaults and solitary confinement are comparable tier-1 custody/facility exposures. This dossier's bathroom law reaches private businesses and carries up to a year, but national hate-crime/employment protections and pending litigation are somewhat broader; the overall level is close to, and slightly below, 0.25-C.

Vellandra excludes visibly trans visitors at the border with no effective remedy but no jail. This dossier's border refusal/fraud risk is narrower, yet the division's criminal bathroom law and abusive custody add jail and severe harm, so it rates below 0.35-A.

Meridia has trained border officers, brief detention, tribunal appeals and compensation. This dossier lacks any working remedy for the facility ban or border fraud finding, and its bathroom law carries jail, so it is far below 0.75-C.
